_comment: Run state for the SEO/AEO routine. Updated each run. Baselines are a cache; the authoritative time series is the committed seo/data/gsc/ files.
_serp_rotation_note: Index selects clusters (excluding aeo-sentinels) in portfolio order: for k in 0..2, cluster[(index+k) % n], query[floor(index/n) % len]. Index 0 covered used-car-to-ebike / new-to-boston / family-logistics. Index 3 covered year-round-weather / town-commuters / ebike-curious. Index 6 covered employers-rto / schools-wellness / local-business-partners. Index 9 covers local-business-partners / brand-navigational / used-car-to-ebike. NOTE: students-campus was inserted at position 4 this run, so the modulus changed from 9 to 12 non-sentinel clusters; the sequence is not comparable to earlier runs and that is fine — the point is coverage over time, not a fixed cycle.

baselines._basis: EXACT. Recomputed 2026-09-08 from the seventeen weekly files containing site_totals (2026-05-09 -> 2026-09-04), asserted contiguous with no overlapping ranges. These INCLUDE the week ending 2026-09-04. Files WITHOUT site_totals are the superseded 2026-08-20 backfill and must be excluded — mixing the series double-counts.
baselines._comparison_baselines_note: The report's 'vs 4-wk / vs 12-wk' columns compare this week AGAINST the trailing means EXCLUDING it: clicks 12.75 / 12.00, impressions 1263.3 / 1035.6. Those are the prior run's cached values, which is why they match seo/reports/2026-08-31.md.
baselines._nonbrand_note: Bucketed non-brand query-dimension impressions (all clusters except brand-navigational, plus unmatched). 48 on 2026-08-24, 49 on 2026-08-31, 284 on 2026-09-08 (computed by scripts/seo/analyze.mjs --section clusters; an earlier hand-computed 258 omitted the 26 unmatched impressions). The jump is the students-campus cluster, which did not exist before this run. THIS IS NOW THE STAGNATION TRIGGER'S BASIS — see seo/methodology.md. Caveat: 284 is one week and one page class; if the campus surge is seasonal it falls back in October.
baselines._posthog_note: Weekly organic sessions, Monday-start weeks, counted as count(DISTINCT properties.$session_id) on $pageview where $referring_domain matches google/bing/duckduckgo/ecosia/yahoo/brave. Excludes mail-security link-scanner sessions (paths matching '%/1/0100%' or '/preferences/%'), which added 9 phantom 'bing.com' sessions in the week of 2026-08-24. Series to 2026-09-08: 35, 29, 35, 25, 32, 24, 29, 35 (most recent first). Small differences from the 2026-08-31 report's numbers come from that report's slightly narrower referrer list; this definition is the one to reuse.
baselines._aeo_referral_note: Zero ChatGPT/Perplexity/Claude/Copilot/Gemini sessions this run, against 2 (ChatGPT) last week and 6 the week before. Those were contest participants asking about /events/shift-your-summer rules; the contest ended. We have never had answer-engine referrals representing discovery.

health._llms_note: /llms.txt is generated per request from approved guides + qualifying towns (src/app/llms.txt/route.ts), so its hash changes whenever content is published. Treat hash drift as expected; the link and section counts are the meaningful drift signals. If SEO item 1 ships, expect sections 5 -> 6 and links 75 -> 88.

watch_list.what: Is the campus surge seasonal? /shift-your-semester pages took 917 impressions (36% of all site impressions) in the week to 2026-09-04, which is exactly when students decide how they will get around. October will show whether students-campus holds or falls away with the start of term.
watch_list.action: Report students-campus impressions every weekly pulse. Do not restate the non-brand discovery baseline as a trend until there are four weeks of it.

watch_list.what: year-round-weather has THREE published guides (mg_biking_in_rain, mg_cold_weather, mg_walking_weather) and zero impressions across every pull. Streetsblog's single 2022 article wins the sentinel query with ~2,000 words, named local riders, and no structured data. Three short scattered guides do not compete with one page like that.
watch_list.action: October: brief a structural fix — one comprehensive local page, or a hub tying the three existing guides together — before the seasonal window opens in November. NOT a fourth guide.

watch_list.what: Drive-time siblings. howlongtowalk.org captures the 10/15/20/30-minute variants with one page each and an on-page conversion table; we capture one query with a prose-only guide.
watch_list.action: October candidate: add a table to the drive-time guide, and consider sibling pages. Wait for the 2026-10-12 read on the guide first.

watch_list.what: The Tufts grad-student guide to getting around Boston without a car now ranks on the 'do you need a car in Boston' sentinel. A university page beating us on our own sentinel, in the week we discovered the campus audience, points at where new-to-boston's opening is.
watch_list.action: Feed into the October look at new-to-boston (33 impressions / 0 clicks over 28 days, avg pos 16.6).

watch_list.what: Drive-time guide shipped 2026-08-31. As of 2026-09-04 it has NOT yet appeared in the page table (four days of data); /commute-advisor (1,052 impr, 2 clicks) and /guides/when-walking-is-faster (955 impr, 1 click) held their volume. No cannibalisation visible yet.
watch_list.action: Report the three pages together in the ledger each week until ~2026-10-12, then call it.

watch_list.what: UTM consolidation is working. Clean rows now appear for cambridge-ma (36), somerville-ma (33), boston-ma (20) — all three were absent from the report last week — and arlington-ma has consolidated onto one URL. Parameterized rows persist (245 impressions this week) and should fade as Google re-crawls.
watch_list.action: Keep watching weekly. If parameterized rows persist past ~2026-10-12, escalate.

resolved_notes.what: The portfolio had no cluster for campus/student transportation queries, so 'bu cycle kitchen', 'mit t pass', 'tufts safe ride' and their siblings bucketed as unmatched noise across two reports — while /shift-your-semester grew into the largest impression surface on the site (917 impressions, 36% of the week).
resolved_notes.fix: Added the students-campus cluster to seo/keyword-portfolio.json, placed BEFORE town-commuters because bucketing takes the first matching cluster and 'boston university bike' would otherwise fall to the town patterns. Tested against 34 real queries: 21 campus queries matched, and somerville/cambridge/bluebikes/brand queries correctly did not. Coverage 69% -> 93%.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not read a zero-impression cluster as an absence of demand without checking the unmatched list against the page table. A page class can become the biggest surface on the site and stay invisible to a ledger that only counts what it has patterns for.

resolved_notes.what: The stagnation trigger read total organic clicks, which brand dominates — the 2026-08-31 run showed the headline up 51% while non-brand discovery impressions were flat (48 -> 49). The trigger would not have fired on a flat discovery trend.
resolved_notes.fix: Changed the trigger's basis to non-brand discovery impressions in seo/methodology.md. Total clicks stay in the ledger; they just do not drive the trigger.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not trigger on total clicks, and do not read non-brand clicks weekly — they run 0-2 and are pure noise at that volume.

resolved_notes.what: Nearly drafted a fourth winter-biking guide for year-round-weather (zero impressions, seasonal window opening). The library already has three weather guides.
resolved_notes.fix: Checked content/micro-guides-library.md before drafting. Redirected the draft to the used-car-to-ebike gap, which had recurring query evidence and no page at all.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not propose a guide for a cluster without first listing what the library already publishes for it. A zero-impression cluster with existing content is a visibility problem, not a content problem.

resolved_notes.what: Dev servers cannot be started from an unattended scheduled run, so the JSON-LD added in SEO item 2 could not be checked in a browser.
resolved_notes.fix: Extracted the FAQ constant and serialized the schema in isolation instead: six questions, valid JSON round-trip, no HTML tags surviving into acceptedAnswer.text, price token resolving to $90. Flagged in the report and email that the rendered page is unverified and worth an eyeball on the Vercel preview.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not claim a rendered-page verification that an unattended run cannot perform. Say what was checked and what was not.

resolved_notes.what: Email 401 on the first attempts. Two different secrets share the name CRON_SECRET: gsi-website/.env.local holds the Vercel cron secret guarding this repo's /api/cron/* routes, while the Supabase edge functions use a separate deployed CRON_SECRET. The Shift project injects the Supabase-side value via an env block in its .claude/settings.local.json, which is why sentry-triage and plg-review (both run from the Shift directory) always worked. gsi-website had no env block, so $CRON_SECRET was empty here.
resolved_notes.fix: Added a matching env block to gsi-website/.claude/settings.local.json (gitignored). Verified: HTTP 200, sent to keith@gogreenstreets.org.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not overwrite CRON_SECRET in .env.local to 'fix' this — that value is correct and in use by six Vercel cron routes.

resolved_notes.what: Branches seo/2026-08-gsc-true-totals and seo/2026-08-portfolio-patterns were cut before a week of unrelated work landed on main, so their diffs against main showed ~125 files and would have reverted the walk-audit and events-calendar commits if merged.
resolved_notes.fix: Rebased both onto main and force-pushed with --force-with-lease. Each is now a clean single-file diff.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not let a proposed branch sit unrebased across a week of main activity — rebase pending seo/ branches at the start of each run before quoting their diffs.

resolved_notes.what: Shipping item 1 re-backfilled 16 weekly files on Saturday-to-Friday windows, but the 16 original Monday-ending files from the 2026-08-20 backfill stayed on disk. The two series overlap, so a naive glob over weekly-*.json would double-count.
resolved_notes.fix: Deleting the superseded files was blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier, so the fix is a selection rule instead: the current series is defined as files containing site_totals, written into seo/methodology.md under the accountability ledger. Verified that selection is contiguous and reproduces the 2026-08-31 baselines exactly.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not glob seo/data/gsc/weekly-*.json without filtering on site_totals. Do not read the level from `totals` — that field is query-dimension and runs ~4x under.

resolved_notes.what: After the migration published the guide, /guides did not list it and llms.txt/sitemap did not include it. sitemap.ts and llms.txt/route.ts both set revalidate = 3600 and self-heal within the hour, but src/app/guides/page.tsx had no revalidate, so the library index was statically baked at build time and would only update on the next deploy.
resolved_notes.fix: Added `export const revalidate = 3600` to src/app/guides/page.tsx to match the sibling files.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not assume a guide is discoverable just because its own /guides/<slug> URL returns 200. After shipping a guide, check the /guides index, sitemap.xml and llms.txt too — the slug route is dynamic and will 200 well before the index catches up.
